name: US Semiconductor
old_description: Upstream Component Strategy for Space, Defense, and Radiation-Exposed Systems
about:
US Semiconductor is headquartered in Palm Bay, Florida. The company operates as a microelectronics component supplier and upstream pathway architect, engaging early in the architecture process to help aerospace, defense, space, and safety-critical programs determine viable semiconductor strategies. No founding year or ownership details are publicly disclosed.

The firm supplies a range of microelectronics component families including memory (EEPROM, UVEPROM, SRAM, serial memory), FPGAs, processors and microcontrollers, analog and power management devices, and interfaces and mixed-signal components. Beyond component supply, US Semiconductor provides engineering services such as qualification strategy alignment, component trade studies, radiation-conscious component strategy, obsolescence and lifecycle planning, and supply chain and sourcing strategy. The company does not operate as a testing laboratory, certification authority, or system integrator.

US Semiconductor serves programs across space systems (satellite platforms, exploration missions, constellation architectures), aerospace and defense (avionics platforms, defense electronics, mission-critical control systems), and industrial and safety-critical systems (infrastructure, energy platforms, transportation control, safety monitoring). Its customers are engineering and program teams facing compressed acquisition cycles, radiation exposure constraints, and long deployment timelines.

The company differentiates itself by engaging upstream before architecture hardens, aligning semiconductor selection with mission exposure, qualification boundaries, and lifecycle continuity. This early pathway determination aims to prevent redesign, delays, and supply disruption during program deployment.
